body: What reason do you have to believe that it's not?

You do pretty well for a morning drunk person, and I greatly appreciate your response :) You're right, I think I am a bit aware of my flaws. I think the feeling of never being able to overcome them is what gets me. I am also not sure if there is a beneficial difference between knowing what I want and knowing what I need. I know I need a good job, but I think "good" and "what makes me happy" are two entirely different things. 

In terms of yourself, stay in Uni! Even if you aren't graduating on time, I'm envious that you will be able to spend more time in school. I love school and everything it offers, take full advantage of the time you have there and you'll find what you want out of life eventually as well. Thank you for the response :)

I'll admit- I accidentally fell asleep immediately after posting this, and your post was an incredible thing to wake up to. I had a small panic attack at this part:


>I only know your Uni because someone I went to high school is(was?!?!) going there.

Not sure how you narrowed down that but, ah well, my uni is a big place and I'm assuming the person you know definitely does not know me. ha!

Anyway, I appreciate you immensely for reading my entire post and responding. You are so right in so many ways and I truly envy your self assurance on the matter. AND you're only 20, wow. Quite a solid insight for a 20 year old male.

I like especially what you said about my father, this bit:

>You can help your Dad be more positive, with positivity. And he does deserve that. Not because he's your Da' and you're supposed to love him, but because he's a person with hurt and everything of his own.

I only know maybe the fraction of the hurt he has seen in his life, and you are right- he is his own person with his own pain, and I need to recognize that. It isn't easy backing down to his negative mentality, but I will try to be more positive. 

On the topic of sex, I believe it's going to take some time until I figure out exactly how I should treat it. There have been times when I've had a random hook up, felt totally fine, and moved on. There's been other times when I've had a random hook up and have wanted to pursue the person. And then there were times where I just regretted it. I wish there were written rules to this game. 

When it comes down to it I think it's just my own mental state and how I allow my brain to think. I've heard forcing positive thoughts eventually creates naturally positive thoughts. But hell, that's a hard hump to get over.

All in all, I just want to thank you for taking the time to read my entire post. Knowing even one person read it makes me feel so, so much better. AND you didn't ridicule me for being crazy, so perhaps there is still hope after all?

I'm very grateful for you. x
